prompt: The temperature of a cup of coffee $t$ minutes after it is poured is $T(t)$ degrees Celsius. You know $T(5) = 70$ and $T'(5) = -3$. Use the tangent line at $t = 5$ to estimate the temperature at $t = 7$ minutes.
hint: $T'(5) = -3$ means: at the $5$-minute mark, the coffee is cooling at about $3$ degrees per minute.

hints.text: $T'(5) = -3$ means: at the $5$-minute mark, the coffee is cooling at about $3$ degrees per minute.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: if something is at $100$ and dropping $2$ per minute, then $1$ minute later it is about $98$. Here the drop is $3$ per minute and the gap is $2$ minutes.
Tangent line: $T(t) \approx T(5) + T'(5)(t - 5) = 70 - 3(t - 5)$. Put in $t = 7$.

explanation: The tangent line at $t = 5$ is $L(t) = T(5) + T'(5)(t - 5) = 70 - 3(t - 5)$.
So the coffee is about $64$ degrees at $7$ minutes. It is an estimate: the real cooling rate slows as the coffee nears room temperature, so the true value is a little above $64$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Units tell the story
steps: $T'(5)$ has units of degrees per minute, so multiplying by $2$ minutes gives degrees: $-3 \times 2 = -6$ degrees.
Start at $70$ and apply the change: $70 - 6 = 64$.
A derivative is a rate, and rate times time is change — that is all a tangent-line estimate is.
